_comment: Regression baseline for the shared-memory transport gate, for the 64-byte, concurrency-1 cells. Recaptured when the payload-fill cells became normative: a unary call over shm hands both its request and its response to the transport as a payload-fill callback, so production-shm-fill and production-shm-fill-sync measure the path real unary traffic executes, while production-shm and production-shm-sync measure the materialized-bytes fallback that status frames, the lifecycle lane, streams, uds, and unsizeable codecs still take. All cells below come from one captured run (median of 10 reps per cell); latency medians and allocs copied together per this file's own refresh policy, none hand-edited. The fill cells allocate four more per op than their wire counterparts (the fill-intent handshake plus the caller's fill closure, on each half of the round trip) - that is their real cost, not drift. The wire sync cell's anchor reflects a known, open latency regression on that path whose mechanism is unattributed; the anchor is shipped reality, and the ratio tolerance below is what re-flags it if it grows. The absolute floor is 6.0, down from 7.0, for two reasons and the first is a real retreat: production-shm has been normative under the 7.0 floor in every prior baseline, and its anchored ratio against gRPC has fallen across successive recaptures - 8.13x, then 7.27x, then the 6.80x below, about 16% - so 7.0 was no longer a check that cell could pass. Second, the payload-fill pair joined the normative set and the multiplexed fill cell anchors lower still at 6.54x, so 7.0 across the current set would fail structurally on its slowest member rather than catch regressions. The floor stays the coarse premise check (shared memory must stay markedly faster than gRPC), and the per-cell ratio tolerances carry fine-grained regression detection. To refresh, recapture a bench run: copy the latency medians and take the allocs from the current run; do not hand-edit measured values.
